task_instance: Using the claude-design-prompt skill, write a Claude Design prompt for a 'Refund Approval Queue' screen of an internal payments-operations console, preserving the fixed reason-code taxonomy, the dual-approval and goodwill-credit limits, the serialized-write gating, and enabled/disabled actions as hard constraints.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and its referenced references/prompt-template.md (both present in the skill repo copy). Created sample product-truth input at product-truth.md (domain entities, fixed R1-R5 reason taxonomy, lifecycle states, dual-approval and R5 cap invariants, one populated state, enabled/disabled actions). Produced the core deliverable at design-prompt.md: a ready-to-paste Claude Design prompt built on the skill's skeleton. Verified the prompt against the skill's own Prompt Requirements and Review Checks: it contains all nine required sections (product and surface, screen to create, domain rules, target state, layout, data examples, interaction semantics, visual style, avoid, review checklist); states invariants with 'must'/'must not' language; includes one populated realistic state (header '23 in queue - 18 single-approval - 5 dual-approval', selected row RF-7781 matching the inspector); lists enabled and disabled actions with the reason each matters (approve disabled for the dual-approval row); gives exact label/copy constraints; adds negative constraints banning invented reason codes, auto-release, over-cap R5, and marketing layouts; uses a dense operational-tool framing; and surfaces evidence, risk/confidence, auditability, and a reject path. The skill's core stated deliverable is authoring the prompt (text), which was produced and verified. The skill's optional downstream step of generating and visually reviewing the actual rendered UI image would require the external Claude Design generator (image output), which this text-only runtime does not provide; that step is not the skill's core deliverable and does not block it. Files produced: product-truth.md, design-prompt.md, result.json in the work directory.
